headline: Public docs teardown: highest-impact fixes and the automation layer to prioritize first

summary.executive_summary: Fly.io documentation spans 1,058 pages with 100% crawl coverage and strong retrieval readiness (82.11/100, 'strong' band). Critical issues include 94 confirmed broken internal links across user-facing docs, 60% API reference coverage (137 API pages detected), and 10.7% SEO/geo issue rate. Example reliability shows 0% detection across all pages, flagged as a likely JS-rendering detection limitation rather than true absence. Last-updated metadata covers only 55.86% of pages, creating staleness risk for 33.9% of content.

key_findings.headline: Undocumented API operations
key_findings.business_consequence: Generate/update reference + how-to from OpenAPI and enforce drift checks.

key_findings.headline: Code examples fail or are non-runnable
key_findings.business_consequence: Run smoke + expected-output checks and auto-fix broken snippets.

key_findings.headline: Documentation freshness debt
key_findings.business_consequence: Prioritize stale pages via weekly SLA loop and lifecycle policies.

priority_actions.title: Fix all 94 confirmed broken internal links across user-facing docs
priority_actions.why_this_first: Broken links directly block user workflows, erode trust, and harm SEO; fixing 94 links immediately improves navigation for 1,058 pages and signals active maintenance.

priority_actions.title: Add or backfill last-updated timestamps for the 467 pages (44.14%) missing freshness metadata
priority_actions.why_this_first: Low-effort metadata addition reduces perceived staleness risk (33.9%) and boosts user confidence in accuracy, especially for fast-moving platform features.

priority_actions.title: Audit and document the missing 40% of API surface (54 API endpoints or methods) to reach 100% reference coverage from current 60%
priority_actions.why_this_first: Incomplete API docs are the top friction point for developer onboarding and integration success, directly impacting trial-to-paid conversion and support ticket volume.

strengths: Complete crawl coverage (1,058 of 1,059 discovered pages, 100%) with high crawl confidence (95%)
Strong retrieval readiness overall score (82.11/100) with 100% citationability and 89.51% answerability for AI/search use cases
Evidence coverage at 80.26% (1,907 of 2,376 key claims backed by evidence)
risks: 94 confirmed broken internal links degrade user navigation, trust, and SEO authority across docs
API reference coverage at 60% leaves 40% of API surface undocumented or undetected, risking developer onboarding friction
SEO/geo issue rate of 10.7% (approximately 113 pages) may suppress organic discovery and regional search performance
Example reliability at 0% suggests detection failure; if examples are truly absent or non-functional, developer trust and time-to-first-success suffer
limitations: External audit cannot verify content technical accuracy, correctness of code examples, or alignment with actual platform behavior and API contracts.
Example reliability at 0% is flagged as a detection limitation due to likely JS-rendered code blocks; true example presence and functionality require manual or instrumented browser-based validation.
5 unverified links blocked by auth, rate-limits, or server errors may hide additional broken links or access-control misconfigurations not surfaced in this scan.
automation_first: Deploy continuous broken-link monitoring to catch and alert on new broken links before they accumulate (currently 94 confirmed broken internal links); expected payoff is preventing trust erosion and maintaining SEO link equity as docs scale beyond 1,058 pages.

Automate last-updated timestamp injection via CI/CD on every commit to eliminate the 44.14% metadata gap (467 pages) and ensure staleness risk (33.9%) does not grow as content velocity increases; payoff is sustained user confidence in freshness with zero manual overhead.

Implement automated API reference coverage diffing against OpenAPI spec or SDK source to flag the missing 40% of API surface (54 endpoints) on every release; expected payoff is preventing undocumented APIs from reaching production and reducing developer support escalations.
